assumptions: Volume state uses calibrated inventory, measured net delivery and reported pump feedback; commands remain separate.
Level mapping uses the declared piecewise-linear calibration and absolute error bound without extrapolation.
Forecasts hold measured deliveries and pump availability constant unless a candidate explicitly changes an eligible control.
Source potential is inferred as measured net delivery plus the frozen commanded curtailment; its future constancy is an assumption.
Redundant readings must have overlapping absolute bounds; the primary value and bound are retained without averaging.

recommendation.explanation: The observed snapshot shows Tank A starting at 80.48 m³ with an effective capacity of 120 m³ and a net positive inflow of ~52 m³/h from source_a plus backup_pump 16 m³/h into treatment, while bypass and truck_route are idle. The 3‑hour forecast without interventions predicts Tank A exceeds capacity at ~0.76 h, making the baseline infeasible. The initial_search_grid (750 combos) and a coarse 16‑candidate batch were screened, but all constraint checks rejected because any flow that reduces the tank‑a violation either cures it by moving volume to tank_b (via bypass) or by curtailing source_a, yet the combined overrides in the evaluated candidates still leave tank_a over‑full or violate the horizon‑wide conservation constraints. No independently validated feasible run exists among the evaluated candidates. Detector coverage is complete (10/10 required sensors present, raw_coverage_complete true) and the active pump‑delivery warning (delivery_error 44 m³/h) confirms the measurement–command mismatch, but no control combination within the available budget and grid bounds was found that simultaneously satisfies the capacity limit and keeps all hard constraints. Therefore no validated advisory response is available; the session must report null with a concise operational explanation.
